data.user_prompt: What tutorials, tools, and research does jasonzhu.ai publish?

sections.text:
JasonZhu.AI publishes three main types of content:

- **Hands-on AI tutorials:** Practical guides for Claude Code, Cursor, AI agents, agent Skills, MCP, vibe coding, website development, prompt engineering, and AI-assisted data analysis. It also publishes a free AI-learning map covering official courses from 10 platforms.[1][2]
- **AI tools and curated resources:** Reviews and explainers for AI products, plus projects such as **Agent Skills Hub**, a directory of security-graded Claude Skills, MCP servers, and agent tools. Its GitHub projects also include video-generation Skills, an AI terminology radar, backlink auditing, and other developer utilities.[1][5]
- **Research and industry analysis:** A daily AI-news digest covering Skills, tools, business/monetization, global expansion, and AI papers. Recent research summaries discuss topics such as robotics, turbulent-flow benchmarks, clinical neuroimaging, research agents, browser automation, and agent-to-frontend protocols.[3][9]
- **Independent-founder and creator guidance:** Documented material on registering and operating a UK company, international growth, SEO and competitor research, creator monetization, and the economics and architecture of building the JasonZhu.AI site.[1][2][4]
- **Prompt and project showcases:** A library of prompts and generated projects, including Three.js games, 3D scenes, motion graphics, and comparisons of models and tools such as Claude, Gemini, Unreal Engine, Blender, and Tripo AI.[4][6][10]

In short, the site combines **practical AI education, tool discovery, open-source projects, AI research summaries, and guidance for building businesses with AI**.
